blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Oral cancer and the oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD) that can precede it are visible on the oral mucosa, which makes smartphone photographs a promising tool for screening. Deep learning models for this task classify individual photographs. However, screening refers patients, not photographs: a patient is usually photographed several times, and the referral decision must miss no more than a set share of patients with disease. We propose OraRefer, a patient-level screening model that reads each photograph with a segmentation-guided foundation model that conditions its class decision on the predicted lesion, combines all photographs of a patient with risk factors, and refers through a threshold with a finite-sample sensitivity guarantee. The model localizes the mouth itself, so inference needs no annotation. On 3000 photographs of 714 patients, patient-level fusion reaches an AUROC of 0.919 and outperforms attention-based multiple-instance learning. At a 90% sensitivity target, OraRefer detects 95% of patients with OPMD or cancer and misses 3 of 61 patients with cancer, at a specificity of 0.610. Because the threshold is calibrated without retraining, each clinic can set its own guaranteed operating point on a local calibration sample.
blocks.zh: 口腔癌和口腔潜在恶性疾病(OPMD)在口腔黏液中可见,这使得智能手机照片成为有希望的筛查工具. 这一任务的深层学习模型将个人照片分类. 然而,筛选指的是病人,而不是照片:病人通常会被拍照几次,转诊决定不得错过不超过一定比例的疾病病人. 我们提议Ora Refer,一种病人一级的筛选模型,它读取每张照片,并配有分块制导的基础模型,以预测的损伤为条件作出分类决定,将病人的所有照片与风险因素结合起来,并通过一个有限度的样本敏感性保障的阈值进行引用。 模型将嘴本身本地化,因此推论不需要注释. 在714名患者的3000张照片中,患者级聚变达到0.919的AUROC,并且超越了基于注意力的多层学习. 在90%的敏感度指标下,Ora Refer检测到95%的OPMD或癌症患者,61名癌症患者中有3人缺失,特异性为0.610. 由于阈值在没有再培训的情况下进行校准,每个诊所都可以在当地校准样本上设定自己的保证操作点.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Cancers of the lip and oral cavity caused 389485 new cases and 188230 deaths worldwide in
2022 [ 1 ] . They can be preceded by oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD), visible mucosal
abnormalities with an increased risk of cancer [ 2 ] . A photograph of the mouth can
therefore show the disease that screening must find, and smartphones bring such photographs within reach of primary
care. The screening decision, however, concerns a patient, not a photograph. A patient is often photographed
several times, carries risk factors such as tobacco and betel quid use [ 3 ] , and must be
referred if any lesion is suspicious [ 4 ] . This calls for a patient-level model whose sensitivity holds on the next patients it sees,
not only on average.

blocks.en:
With the release of public datasets, deep learning on oral photographs has advanced. The dataset of Piyarathne et
al. [ 5 ] provides 3000 smartphone photographs of 714
patients with lesion polygons and risk factors. On these data, classifiers have used convolutional and transformer
backbones [ 6 ] , oral-cavity segmentation followed by image–metadata
fusion [ 7 ] , embedding-level fusion with clinical data [ 8 ] , and
stacked ensembles with per-patient posterior smoothing [ 9 ] . Two of these studies [ 6 , 8 ] split the data by image, which places photographs of one patient in both the training and the test set. More importantly, none
of them turns all photographs of a patient into one referral decision with controlled sensitivity. General tools exist
for each half of the problem: attention-based multiple-instance learning pools instances into a bag
label [ 10 ] , including patients in oral cytology [ 11 ] , and conformal and Neyman–Pearson thresholds bound the errors of a fixed
classifier [ 12 , 13 ] , with conformal triage applied to medical
imaging [ 14 ] . A patient-level bound, however, requires out-of-sample patient scores at both
stages of the model.

blocks.en:
We propose OraRefer, a screening model that goes from a patient’s raw photographs to a referral with
guaranteed sensitivity (Fig. 1 ). First, we introduce a
segmentation-guided image model: one network, trained jointly to segment the mouth and the lesion and to classify the
photograph, that conditions its class decision on the predicted lesion. Where earlier work segments the oral cavity in
a separate preprocessing network [ 7 ] , our segmentation training shapes the features the
classifier reads, and the same network crops the mouth from the full frame, so no annotation is needed at test time. Second, we introduce a patient-level referral
layer that fuses all photographs of a patient with risk factors and refers through a distribution-free sensitivity
threshold and Mondrian conformal triage, both calibrated on held-out patients without retraining. Third, we show on
714 patients that OraRefer outperforms frozen foundation-model probes, untrained aggregation, and attention-based multiple-instance learning, and detects 95% of patients with OPMD or cancer,
including 58 of 61 with cancer, against a 90% target.

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en:
OraRefer has three parts (Fig. 1 ). An image model reads each photograph in two passes and returns
class probabilities, a lesion mask, and an uncertainty estimate. A fusion model turns the outputs for all photographs
of a patient, together with the patient’s risk factors, into one score. A threshold calibrated on held-out patients
then turns the score into a referral. We call a patient referable if any of their photographs shows OPMD or cancer.
blocks.zh:
Ora Refer有三个部分(图1). 图像模型将每张相片分为两段并返回
类概率、损伤口罩和不确定性估计。 组合模型将所有照片的输出转换
与病人的风险因素一分为一。 对被扣留的病人进行阈值校正
然后把分数变成推荐 如果有照片显示 OPMD 或癌症,我们叫病人可参考。

boundaries ( λ cls = 0.5 \lambda_{\mathrm{cls}}=0.5 , λ con = 0.1 \lambda_{\mathrm{con}}=0.1 , λ raa = 0.05 \lambda_{\mathrm{raa}}=0.05 ). ℒ aux \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{aux}} holds decaying auxiliary losses on an
intermediate decoder output and a second classifier head, and a term that ties the healthy-class probability to the
predicted lesion area.

blocks.en: 2.2 Self-Localization at Test Time
blocks.zh: 2.2 在试验时自行本地化

blocks.en:
Training mixes full frames with mouth crops, so the model also reads uncropped photographs. At test time, a first pass
on the full frame predicts the mouth mask, whose bounding box, padded by 8%, is the crop for the
second pass. Inference therefore needs no annotation.

第二传. 因此,无需作说明。

blocks.en: 3 Experiments
blocks.zh: 3个实验

blocks.en: 3.1 Data and Protocol
blocks.zh: 3.1 数据和协议

blocks.en:
We use the dataset of Piyarathne et al. [ 5 ] : 3000 photographs of
714 patients, taken with mobile phones by dental surgeons at a teaching hospital in Sri Lanka.
Under the supervision of oral medicine specialists, each photograph is labeled healthy (729),
benign (748), OPMD (1394), or cancer (129) and annotated
with mouth and lesion polygons. Histopathology confirmed all cancer and 56.4% of OPMD diagnoses [ 5 ] . Each patient has a median of four photographs
(range 1–18) and records of age, sex, and three binary risk factors.
381 patients are referable, 61 of them with cancer, and 333 are not.
blocks.zh:
我们使用Piyaratne等人的数据集。 [5]: 3000张照片
714名患者,由牙科外科医生在斯里兰卡的一所教学医院用手机接诊.

All results come from patient-level five-fold cross-validation stratified by patient category and risk factors.
Two patient pairs share an identical photograph; each pair stays in one fold and one calibration part. All model selection happens inside the training
folds. The image model uses one configuration for all folds; inside each training set, 17% of
patients are held out to select the checkpoint, the temperature, and the lesion-mask threshold, and the fusion penalty
is chosen by inner cross-validation. The image model trains for 20 epochs at 448 px with batch size 16, AdamW, and base learning
rate 3 × 10 − 4 3\times 10^{-4} , on a 16 GB V100. Thresholds target τ = 0.90 \tau=0.90 with δ = 0.05 \delta=0.05 , and triage uses α = 0.05 \alpha=0.05 . The 25 calibration sets hold 60–62
referable patients each, 8–12 of them with cancer, and triage shares are averaged over 20 random calibration re-splits of
each fold.

blocks.en: 3.2 Comparisons and Metrics
blocks.zh: 3.2 比较和计量

blocks.en:
At the image level, removing segmentation guidance yields a DINOv2 classifier fine-tuned on the same predicted crops with the same schedule, without segmentation losses, lesion-guided pooling, or region-affinity attention. We also remove
lesion-guided pooling, region-affinity attention, or supervised contrastive learning alone, give the second pass the
annotated mouth box, and train linear probes on frozen full-photograph DINOv2-B , DINOv2-L , and SigLIP2 [ 22 ] .

由损伤引导的集合、区域关注或单独监督的对比性学习,给予第二次通过
注释口盒,在被冻结的全相机DINov2-B,DINov2-L,和SigLIP2[22]上进行线性探测.

blocks.en:
Patient-level baselines form three groups: logistic regression on image features or risk factors alone; untrained aggregation by the maximum, mean, and noisy-OR of q i ​ j q_{ij} ; and trained learners: gradient boosting, late-fusion networks with and without gating by image uncertainty, and ABMIL [ 10 ] and
CAR-MIL [ 23 ] . The attention models receive the same per-photograph outputs and risk factors plus
the first 32 principal components of frozen DINOv2-B embeddings of the full photograph, and CAR-MIL adds a counterfactual attention regularizer
to ABMIL. Like OraRefer, every trained baseline is Platt-calibrated, and the neural ones stop early on internal
validation patients.

blocks.en: 4.1 Image Model
blocks.zh: 4.1 图像模型

blocks.en:
Segmentation guidance drives the image model (Table 1 ). OraRefer reaches a four-class macro AUROC of
0.893 and a macro-F1 of 0.704. This exceeds the best published four-class result under
patient-grouped evaluation, a macro-F1 of 0.662 on a curated subset of 2438 photographs cropped to the
lesion [ 9 ] , whereas OraRefer reads all 3000 photographs uncropped. OraRefer also outperforms the frozen foundation-model probes by
0.069–0.084 in macro AUROC. Without segmentation guidance, macro AUROC falls by
0.023 on the same crops. The drop is consistent across all five folds, at five times the seed-to-seed change. Lesion-guided pooling accounts for 0.009 of this drop and the segmentation
training for the rest, and supervised contrastive learning adds a further 0.007; pooling and
contrastive learning each help in four of five folds. Region-affinity attention raises lesion Dice from
0.561 to 0.580. The gain from segmentation guidance carries through to the referral decision. For each ablated
image model, we refit the fusion model on its out-of-fold outputs, a single level of cross-fitting under which the full
model reaches 0.913 instead of 0.919. Removing segmentation guidance lowers patient AUROC
to 0.894 (DeLong p = 0.005 p=0.005 ),
four times the patient-level seed-to-seed change (0.005), whereas no other component changes it by more than 0.008.

blocks.en: 4.2 Patient-Level Fusion
blocks.zh: 4.2 患者级融合

blocks.en:
Learned fusion outperforms untrained pooling of the photograph scores (Table 2 ). Even without risk
factors, the image-only model reaches an AUROC of 0.909, above the untrained aggregates
(DeLong p ≤ 0.005 p\leq 0.005 ). Risk factors add information beyond the photographs, which a likelihood-ratio
test of adding them to a logistic model of the image-only score confirms ( χ 2 ​ ( 5 ) = 34.4 \chi^{2}(5)=34.4 , p < 0.001 p<0.001 ), and with them OraRefer reaches
0.919, the highest AUROC in Table 2 , above each untrained aggregate (DeLong p < 0.001 p<0.001 ). It outperforms ABMIL and CAR-MIL by 0.029 ( p = 0.001 p=0.001 each,
Holm-adjusted over 13 comparisons with the other trained models in Table 2 and
six variants of OraRefer), although both attention models also receive frozen DINOv2 embeddings, and at the
guaranteed sensitivity it reaches a specificity of 0.610, compared with 0.562 for image
evidence alone and 0.508 for ABMIL. More flexible learners do not improve on the calibrated logistic
regression: gradient boosting reaches 0.916, and the late-fusion network 0.915, or
0.909 when gated by image uncertainty. Neither photograph counts nor the four-model test scoring drive
these results: count-free summaries (means and fractions) give 0.912, and scoring each test patient,
like each training patient, with a single image model (trained on the four training folds) gives 0.917, both above every untrained aggregate and attention model.

triage refers 29% of patients directly, sends 39%
to clinician review, and returns 32% to routine care, which receives 5.1%
of referable patients (4.3%–6.3% over re-splits), consistent with α = 0.05 \alpha=0.05 (Fig. 2 (c)).

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
OraRefer turns a patient’s raw smartphone photographs into a referral with guaranteed sensitivity. Segmentation
guidance drives its image model, and self-localization removes the need for test-time annotation. Patient-level
fusion with risk factors outperforms untrained aggregation and attention-based multiple-instance learning. Since
the thresholds are calibrated without retraining, a new clinic can set its own guaranteed
operating point from a representative local sample of patients with OPMD or cancer. These retrospective results motivate prospective evaluation in community screening.
blocks.zh:
Ora Refer将病人的原始智能手机照片转换成有保证敏感性的转诊。 分块
引导驱动其图像模型,自我本地化消除了测试时间注释的需要. 患者级别
与风险因素的结合比未经培训的聚合和基于注意力的多层次学习要好。 自兹
在不进行再培训的情况下调整门槛,新的诊所可以确定自己的保障
操作点来自当地有代表性的OPMD或癌症患者样本. 这些回顾性结果促使在社区筛查中进行预期评估。
